editorial:
Two years after the Fourth Great Ninja War, the moon starts falling toward Earth, and a strange enemy named Toneri wants Hinata. When he takes Hanabi instead, Naruto and friends rush to rescue her and save the world. The movie mixes big ninja action with a sweet, slow-burn romance, giving long-time fans a payoff while keeping the story easy to follow. You get familiar faces, high stakes, and a softer side of Naruto that makes the whole adventure feel personal.

The fights are flashy, the animation looks sharp, and the emotional beats land well, especially for Naruto and Hinata fans. Some side characters get less screen time, and the villain can feel a bit flat. Still, if you want closure and romance, this is a really great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final battle, Naruto and Hinata work together to stop Toneri and the falling moon. Toneri is defeated, Hanabi is rescued, and the moon is pushed back into place. After years of missed chances, Naruto finally confesses his feelings to Hinata, and the movie ends with their wedding, showing the couple starting a happy future together with their friends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves anime romance and ninja action.
